lines.text: Earns 5% a year on all the money it uses
lines.why: For every ₹100 of shareholders' money and loans in the business, it made ₹5 of operating profit last year (better than 5% of Metals & mining). Past years: up and down; recent trend declining. Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 15, weak < 10 (default rule, all sectors).

lines.text: Keeps ₹3 of every ₹100 of sales as operating profit
lines.why: Operating margin 2.6% (better than 5% of Metals & mining). Past years: up and down; recent trend declining. Colour from close peers (Steel (Metals & Mining), 32 stocks): middle half 6.68–14.5 (band rule PROXY).
For every ₹100 of shareholders' money, it has borrowed ₹27 (better than 61% of Metals & mining). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≤ 0.5, weak > 1 (default rule, all sectors).
For every ₹1 of interest it pays, it earns ₹2.5 of operating profit (better than 17% of Metals & mining). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 5, weak < 3 (default rule, all sectors).

lines.text: Profit is not fully turning into cash
lines.why: For every ₹100 of reported profit in recent years, ₹-149 actually came in as cash (better than 1% of Metals & mining). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 0.8, weak < 0.5 (default rule, all sectors).

valuation.text: Price tag: pricier than its close peers
valuation.why: The whole business costs 24× its yearly operating cash profit (EBITDA). Colour from close peers (Steel (Metals & Mining), 32 stocks): middle half 9.35–23.7 (band rule PROXY).

flags.text: Check: the accounts resemble past earnings-manipulation cases (Beneish M-score)
flags.why: M-score -0.72 is above the −1.78 line. This is a statistical hint, not proof, and the score is not yet validated on Indian companies: read the annual report's notes on receivables, margins and cash flow before trusting the profits.

flags.text: Profit is running well ahead of cash coming in
flags.why: (Profit − operating cash flow) is 13.6% of total assets; above 10% is a warning.
Only ₹-149 of cash came in for every ₹100 of reported profit over recent years (below ₹50 is a red flag).

flags.text: Thinly traded – hard to buy or sell without moving the price
flags.why: Typical day: about ₹2.4 crore traded (we exclude below ₹5 crore).

fund.note: Trap: a very low PE at the top of the metal cycle usually signals the peak, not a bargain.

lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: would probably pass (2 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: For every ₹100 it owes within a year, it holds ₹180 of cash, stock and dues coming in.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹50 cr vs working capital ₹285 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years
ch.r: Positive earnings in each of the last 10 years
ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: NSE corporate actions not fetched.

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved -76%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹29 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.
